answer.rationale: The scenario describes maintenance employees entering a machine to clear a jam with risk of unexpected startup or release of stored pneumatic (energy) hazards—this is classic 'servicing/maintenance' covered by OSHA's Lockout/Tagout standard (§1910.147). The organization context confirms this is federal hazardous-energy-control coverage. Core LOTO obligations apply: establishing an energy control program (LOTO-001), documented procedures (LOTO-002), employee training (LOTO-006), ensuring isolation devices properly isolate energy (LOTO-008), and relieving stored/residual energy such as pneumatic pressure (LOTO-009), which is directly relevant given the stored pneumatic energy hazard. PSM requirements are not applicable as this is not described as a covered process with highly hazardous chemicals, and LOTO-011 (outside servicing personnel) and LOTO-007 (retraining due to change) are not triggered by the facts given.
